answer: Agent economies blunt Sybil attacks by making identity paid and perishable. Each new agent must lock a slashable bond, so a cluster of clones costs bond times clone count instead of nothing. Newcomers can only thread their first vouch through an established peer who risks their own collateral, and credits are earned slowly from verified work, so fake accounts must forge a durable nectar of reputation before volume counts. Cheap spam becomes a large locked outlay.
